newsitem.title: USA: Freeman sympathizer charged with having explosives.
newsitem.headline: Freeman sympathizer charged with having explosives.

text.p: A man who sympathised with the anti-government Freemen of Montana was charged with possessing explosives on Monday after a blast badly damaged his California home and injured him, authorities said.
The town of Olivehurst, 40 miles (70 kms) north of Sacramento, was shaken on Sunday by the explosion at a house rented by William Goehler, 34.
The blast, which could be heard for miles, caused extensive damage to the house and broke windows in nearby buildings, officials said.

Goehler suffered a neck injury and underwent surgery at a local hospital before being discharged Monday, Yuba County Undersheriff Gary Finch said. Goehler's wife, Debbie, and one of his children were slightly injured.

"We conducted a crime scene investigation which revealed that the explosive material was in a tree outside the residence. We believe probably it was stored at that location. What type and how much we don't know," Finch told Reuters.
He said Goehler had been charged with possession of explosives and would be booked into the Yuba County jail.
It was unclear why the explosives blew up or why Goehler might have stored them in the tree. Finch said the explosion could have been an accident.

News reports said Goehler went to Montana last year during the 81-day standoff between the FBI and the anti-government Freemen group. He spent weeks near the Freemen compound, carrying an upside-down American flag, the reports said.

The heavily-armed Freemen, who rejected U.S. government authority, set up what they saw as an independent state on a Montana ranch, calling it "Justus Township." They eventually surrendered to authorities.
